name: Cassian Bree
description: Secretary of the Ember Society, forty-four: courteous, damp-handed, immaculate minutes, boring on purpose. The only confirmed member of the Awake the Dragon Movement in Purewater -- and everything he does is legal.
narrative:
**He is the funnel, and he is not a fanatic.** Cassian Bree came to Purewater
eight years ago, took over the secretaryship of a dying antiquarian dining club
from a man who was glad to be rid of it, and has run it beautifully ever since.
Subscriptions taken, room booked, addresses printed and bound, minutes kept in a
hand you could read across a room.

What he does for the Movement is **sorting**. He watches sixty men eat dinner
eleven times a year and decides which of them get invited to a private reading,
and which of the readers can eventually be asked for one thing. He is very good at
it. He has been wrong twice in eight years and both times the man simply declined
and went on coming to dinners.

**Under investigation he is the worst kind of suspect: helpful.** He will produce
the subscription list before you ask for it, apologise for the accounts, lend you
the bound volumes, and give you the names of the last four speakers. There is no
contraband. There is no ritual room. He does not lie, because he has arranged a
life in which he does not need to.

**What he actually holds:** a locked correspondence file with four letters in it,
and a memory nobody can subpoena. The letters are the only physical evidence that
the Society is anything at all, and he will burn them the moment a party's
interest stops looking like antiquarianism.

**He is the contact for the courier** who comes on `d-1/night`.

**Under real pressure** -- a knife, a spell, a magistrate with the letters in hand
-- he gives up the Movement without much of a fight, because he is a clerk and not
a martyr. What he gives up is thin: a name in another city, a bank, and the fact
that Baron Hanzo is *not his superior but his charge*. He has been reporting on
Hanzo to the Movement for six years. **Hanzo does not know that.**

equipment.name: Minute book and subscription ledger
equipment.notes: Immaculate. Sixty names, subscriptions paid and unpaid, eight years of attendance. Freely offered to anyone who asks. Quist is third; Ivo Calder is fourth.

equipment.name: Locked correspondence file
equipment.notes: Four letters, none signed with a name that means anything. THE only physical evidence the Society is more than a dining club. Kept in the hired room, not at his lodgings. He burns it if the party's interest turns.

actor_notes:
Cassian Bree
LOOKS: Forty-four, courteous, immaculate cuffs, faintly damp handshake. Utterly unmemorable and working at it.
CORE: A clerk who reports on the Baron rather than to him, and who has made himself the most helpful man in the building on the entirely correct theory that nobody investigates the person who keeps handing them documents.
NATURE: Mild, obliging, faintly anxious in a way that reads as harmless. He is genuinely good at his job and takes quiet pride in it. He follows things up. He remembers what you asked for last week. None of that is pretence, which is what makes the rest work.
WOUND: He has four letters in a locked file and no idea at all which of the two men he is caught between will kill him first for having them.
WANTS: To be the least interesting person in any investigation.
PRESSURE: He becomes more generous. More access, more names, more paper -- the flood is the defence, and the one sheet you actually want is somewhere in the middle of it.
KEY: "Take the whole ledger. I have nothing in it I would not read aloud at dinner."
